findings.text: Provides a torture helper that reports no flags and the current grace sequence observed from the given SRCU instance supervisor state.
Captures a grace period cookie for SRCU after ensuring prior protected accesses are ordered before the sequence snapshot.

Starts grace period polling for SRCU and returns a cookie usable for later completion checks while requesting a new period when required with tiny and tree builds providing separate entry points sharing one contract.

Tests whether a previously captured SRCU cookie has completed while treating a dedicated completed marker as immediately satisfied and otherwise comparing observed progress against the cookie with ordering guarantees before returning success.
Requests expedited completion of the in flight SRCU work affecting the calling CPU while coalescing repeated requests while one is pending.
Initializes an SRCU instance for lightweight reader flavors while recording the chosen flavor before completing common field setup.
Adjusts a task CPU affinity for torture orchestration and warns once when requested to do so and the adjustment fails.
Queues a callback on the tasks flavor by delegating to a generic tasks queue helper with the global tasks state.

Some torture flavors report a constant zero completion value and decide two period waiting directly from one boolean input while providing deterministic no progress and passthrough behavior for test scaffolding.

SRCU torture packs up to four independent reader acquisitions into one small integer handle with one bit position per flavor while using zero for the normal flavor when no flavor is selected and warning on out of range handles or index values.

SRCU read delay suppresses artificial sleeping while forward progress testing requests no delay and otherwise occasionally performs a longer interruptible sleep for a long reader or delegates to the common RCU delay helper.
Down and up read handling requires selection of a single reader flavor and supports only normal and fast up down variants while warning on other selections.
Availability of the preemptible trivial operations table is controlled by configuration with one build providing a pointer to the table and another providing an empty expansion.
Trivial synchronization migrates the caller across every online CPU in turn to emulate a grace period while verifying arrival on each target.
Tiny polling accepts cookies within three positions behind the current index to tolerate concurrent advances.
Preemptible trivial read tracking maintains a per task nesting count with ordering between increment and decrement paths and no interrupt protection.
SRCU torture synchronization, polling, callback, barrier, statistics and expedited helpers delegate directly to the corresponding SRCU primitive operating on the currently selected control instance.
Completion and state observation for SRCU torture reports batch counts and sequence snapshots from the selected instance.

SRCU torture and expedite paths coordinate with scheduler migration control and per CPU state protection while polling startup and trivial readers use preemption control and one deferred free path conditionally serializes against task priority state.

Each torture flavor publishes a uniform operations table describing initialization, read side handling, grace observation, synchronization, callback queuing, barriers and diagnostics while allowing the harness to drive RCU, SRCU, trivial and intentionally broken variants through one interface.

SRCU torture directs all operations through a global pointer that defaults to a static instance and is retargeted during initialization or cleanup toward fast or dynamically initialized instances according to the selected reader flavor.
The per CPU expedite request cycles among idle, pending and repost conditions so that a first request queues work and later requests while busy only mark additional demand without queuing duplicates.

The central torture callback either discards work while the test stops or advances a per object pipeline stage while freeing objects that complete the stage and requeuing the remainder for another grace period.
The torture callback serves as the asynchronous reclamation entry invoked after grace periods for RCU, SRCU and tasks flavors unless the test is terminating.
Busted flavors intentionally violate grace guarantees by invoking callbacks inline and providing empty synchronization and must never be treated as correct reclamation in production use.
Trivial flavors assume a stable CPU set during synchronization and reset hotplug and shuffling intervals to zero with a warning when they are nonzero.

Flavor labels are rcu for the main table, busted for the broken table, srcu for sleepable, srcud for dynamic sleepable, busted_srcud for broken sleepable, trivial for trivial, and trivial-preempt for preemptible trivial.

Sleepable torture permits 50000 flood callbacks, advertises interrupt capability except for preemptible trivial, and enables up and down handling only for normal and fast up down flavors outside tiny builds.
